moray: A green moray eel, thick muscular olive-green body, mouth open showing sharp teeth, coiled among rocks
swordfish: A swordfish, sleek steel-blue streamlined body, long flat sword-like bill, tall dorsal fin, swimming
marlin: A blue marlin, sleek cobalt-blue streamlined body, long spear-like bill, tall crested dorsal fin, swimming
anglerfish: A deep-sea anglerfish, a rounded globular blackish fish with a huge upturned mouth crammed with long thin needle-like fangs, small dull eyes, and a single thin flexible rod curving forward from its forehead tipped with a SMALL round glowing bulb, a modest pale lure about the size of its eye. The lure is a small glowing bead on a slender stalk, not a large moon-sized sphere
barracuda: A great barracuda seen from the side, an extremely long slender torpedo-shaped fish, narrow and snake-like along its whole length, with a pointed head, a prominent jutting underslung lower jaw showing long uneven fangs, silvery flanks with a few scattered dark blotches, and two widely separated small dorsal fins. Long and lean, not a deep-bodied tuna shape
grouper: A goliath grouper, massive mottled brown-yellow bulky body, wide mouth, hovering near a reef
oarfish: An oarfish, an immensely long ribbon-shaped fish, flattened side to side and many times longer than it is deep, rippling like a silver band, with brilliant silver skin, a crimson-red fin running the entire length of its back, and a crest of long trailing crimson rays streaming up from the top of its head like a plume. Ribbon-thin and enormously elongated
sunfishmola: An ocean sunfish (mola mola) seen from the side, shaped like a giant flattened DISC, an almost circular slab of a body that looks like a huge swimming head abruptly cut off at the back, with no proper tail at all, ending instead in a short ruffled rudder frill. A very tall pointed dorsal fin stands straight up and a matching anal fin hangs straight down, giving a tall lopsided outline. Rough silvery-grey skin and a small round eye and beaked mouth. It must be a round flattened disc with a chopped-off rear, not an ordinary streamlined fish or shark shape
flyingfish: A flying fish gliding above the water, a slender silvery-blue fish with a pair of greatly enlarged stiff wing-like pectoral fins spread wide and flat like glider wings, and a deeply forked tail whose LOWER lobe is distinctly longer than the upper. Streamlined body, large round eye
mandarin_dragonet: A mandarin dragonet, small body covered in intricate wavy blue orange and green patterns, swimming near coral rubble
coelacanth: A coelacanth seen from the side, a heavy steel-blue fish flecked with irregular white-cream spots, whose paired fins are carried on thick fleshy muscular STALKS projecting out from the body like stubby little limbs rather than joining flat to the flank, and whose tail is distinctly THREE-LOBED: an upper lobe and a lower lobe with a small extra pointed middle lobe sticking out from the centre between them. The limb-like stalked fins and the three-lobed tail are essential: it must not be drawn as a shark or an ordinary fish
axolotl: An axolotl seen from the side, a pale pink aquatic salamander with a long body held horizontal and its belly close to the ground, a wide flat head, feathery pink external gill fronds branching from behind the head, four small weak limbs and a long finned tail. Lying flat on all four legs, not upright, not standing on two legs, not humanoid.
seahorse: A seahorse, curled prehensile tail gripping a strand of seagrass, tubular snout, upright posture, ridged bony body
leafyseadragon: A leafy sea dragon, whose entire body is smothered in an elaborate profusion of long ornate LEAF-SHAPED skin appendages sprouting in every direction from its head, neck, back, belly and tail, broad flat golden-green fronds like drifting torn seaweed, so many that the animal's outline is almost lost inside them and it reads as a floating clump of weed. A long thin tubular snout and a straight tail held out behind. It must be buried in leafy fronds, not a plain smooth seahorse with a curled tail
weedyseadragon: A weedy sea dragon, an elongated pipefish-like animal with a long slender straight body held horizontally and a long STRAIGHT tapering tail that does not curl or grip, a long thin tubular snout, small scattered leaf-like appendages along the back and belly, and brilliant colouring: reddish-purple skin covered in small bright yellow spots crossed by silver-blue bands. It is not a seahorse: its tail must be straight, never curled into a spiral
pipefish: A pipefish, extremely slender elongated tubular body, tiny fins, tubular snout, resting among seagrass
moonjelly: A moon jelly, a translucent pale bell shaped like a smooth flattened saucer, carrying four distinct pinkish-violet HORSESHOE-shaped rings clearly visible through the top of the bell, and fringed all around its rim with a dense curtain of hundreds of very short fine hair-like tentacles like a delicate fringe, plus four short frilly oral arms hanging beneath. The tentacles are a fine short fringe around the whole rim, not a few long trailing strands
boxjelly: A box jellyfish, a transparent pale blue bell that is roughly CUBE-shaped but soft and organic, with four flat faces and gently rounded corners and edges, like a translucent squared-off lantern of living jelly. From each of the four bottom corners hangs a separate bundle of several long fine trailing tentacles. Soft and gelatinous, not a hard geometric ice cube and not a solid box
lionsmane: A lion's mane jellyfish, a large reddish-orange domed bell beneath which hangs an enormous dense MASS of hundreds upon hundreds of fine hair-like tentacles, gathered in thick trailing clusters so numerous and tangled that they form a great shaggy flowing mane many times longer than the bell itself, plus broad ruffled crimson oral arms. The sheer density of the tentacle mane is essential, not a few sparse strands
octopus: A giant Pacific octopus, reddish-brown mottled bulbous head, eight long arms lined with suckers, arms curling outward
mimicoctopus: A mimic octopus, brown and white banded body, long thin arms extended in a flattened display, resting on sandy sea floor
cuttlefish: A cuttlefish, a broad flattened oval mantle rimmed by a single continuous undulating FIN running in an unbroken skirt down both sides of the body from front to back, with two large prominent eyes carrying distinctive W-shaped horizontal pupils, eight short arms held together beneath the head, and mottled banded skin in shifting brown and cream. The continuous side-fin skirt and the W-shaped pupils are essential: it is not an octopus and not a squid
giantsquid: A giant squid, massive elongated reddish body, huge eyes, two long feeding tentacles among eight arms, swimming in deep dark water
nautilus: A chambered nautilus, coiled tan-and-white striped shell, numerous small tentacles surrounding the mouth, swimming near a reef
coconutcrab: A coconut crab, a gigantic heavy land crab with a thick domed carapace and immensely thick powerful legs built to carry great weight, one enormous heavy claw much larger than the other, held raised, and long stalked eyes. Deep blue-purple and orange armour plating. Massive and heavy-limbed, the largest land crab in the world, not a small delicate beach crab
fiddlercrab: A fiddler crab, a small crab with one absurdly OVERSIZED bright orange claw nearly as large as its entire body, held up in front of it like a violin, and one tiny insignificant claw on the other side barely visible by comparison. A small squarish olive-brown carapace and long stalked eyes. The extreme mismatch between the huge claw and the tiny one is the whole point
hermitcrab: A hermit crab, spotted orange-red claws and legs protruding from a spiraled shell it carries, standing on a beach
spidercrab: A Japanese spider crab, small round body with extremely long thin spindly legs, standing on the sea floor
lobster: An American lobster seen from the side, a long dark blue-green armoured body lying low and horizontal, two large asymmetric front claws held out in front along the ground, eight jointed walking legs beneath the body, a fan tail behind, and two long antennae. A low-bodied arthropod, not upright, no torso, not standing on two legs, not humanoid.
mantisshrimp: A peacock mantis shrimp, a vividly coloured elongated segmented crustacean in brilliant emerald green with orange and blue banding, whose two raptorial arms are folded up beneath its head like a praying mantis, each ending in a heavy club, and whose two large compound eyes sit out on separate movable STALKS projecting from the head and pointing in different directions. A fan-shaped tail in orange and blue. The folded mantis arms and the stalked swivelling eyes are essential: it must not be a plain lobster or prawn
scarletmacaw: A scarlet macaw, vivid red plumage with yellow and blue wing feathers, bare white face patch, large curved beak, perched on a branch
hyacinthmacaw: A hyacinth macaw, vivid deep cobalt-blue plumage, bright yellow eye ring and lower beak patch, large curved beak, perched on a branch
bluegoldmacaw: A blue-and-gold macaw, bright blue back and wings with a golden-yellow chest, bare white face with fine feather lines, perched on a branch
militarymacaw: A military macaw, olive-green plumage, red forehead patch, blue-tipped wings, perched on a branch
africangrey: An African grey parrot, dense grey feathers with scalloped edges, bright red tail feathers, dark beak, perched on a branch
cockatoo: A sulphur-crested cockatoo, white plumage, tall curved yellow crest raised, dark beak, perched on a branch
blackcockatoo: A red-tailed black cockatoo, glossy black plumage, red panels in the tail feathers, tall crest, perched on a branch
cockatiel: A cockatiel, grey plumage, bright yellow crested head, orange cheek patches, perched on a branch
budgie: A budgerigar, vivid green and yellow plumage with black scalloped markings on the back, perched on a branch
lorikeet: A rainbow lorikeet, vivid blue head, green back and wings, orange-red chest, perched on a flowering branch
kea: A kea, olive-green plumage, bright orange underwing feathers, curved grey beak, standing on a rocky alpine ledge
kakapo: A kakapo, a large heavy flightless parrot with moss-green and yellow mottled plumage, a broad rounded face with a fine bristly facial disc, and a short pale hooked parrot beak curving down over the chin. It is a parrot, not an owl: no ear tufts, no feather horns on the head, and a thick parrot beak rather than a raptor beak. Standing on two sturdy grey legs. Plain empty white background: no bowl, no tank, no water, no straw, no ground, no scenery behind the animal.
eclectus: An eclectus parrot, vivid emerald green plumage with a bright orange beak, standing on a branch
conure: A sun conure, brilliant yellow-orange plumage with green wing tips, perched on a branch
rosella: A crimson rosella, deep red plumage with blue cheek patches and blue-black scalloped wings, perched on a branch
quakerparrot: A monk parakeet, green plumage with a pale grey face and chest, perched on a branch
baldeagle: A bald eagle perched on a branch, a large dark chocolate-brown eagle with a pure white head and neck and a pure white tail, and a very large heavy hooked bright yellow bill deep from top to bottom, with a heavy brow ridge over a pale yellow eye giving a fierce frowning expression, and yellow feet. The massive deep yellow bill and the clean white head and tail are essential
goldeneagle: A golden eagle perched on a rock, a large eagle whose body is uniformly deep rich dark brown, with a distinct shawl of lance-shaped GOLDEN-TAWNY feathers over the back of the crown and nape catching the light, a dark grey hooked bill slimmer than a sea eagle's, and fully feathered legs with golden trousers of feathering running all the way down to the toes. The dark brown body with only the nape golden, and the fully feathered legs, are essential: its head must not be pale blonde all over
harpyeagle: A harpy eagle, dark grey back, pale barred underside, large double crest raised on the head, massive talons, perched on a branch
philippineeagle: A Philippine eagle, shaggy brown-and-white crest feathers, pale underside, large blue-grey beak, perched on a branch
stellerseagle: A Steller's sea eagle perched, a huge blackish-brown eagle with a MASSIVE deep bright orange-yellow hooked bill, by far the largest and heaviest bill of any eagle, dominating its head, with bold white shoulders forming large white patches along the leading edge of each wing, white feathered thighs and a white wedge-shaped tail. The enormous orange bill and the white shoulder patches are essential
peregrine: A peregrine falcon, slate-grey back, barred white underside, black hooded head marking, perched on a cliff ledge
osprey: An osprey, dark brown back, white underside and head with a dark eye stripe, perched near water with talons gripping a branch
redtailhawk: A red-tailed hawk, mottled brown back, pale streaked chest, distinctive brick-red tail, perched on a branch
harrier: A northern harrier in flight, a slender raptor with long narrow wings held raised in a shallow V dihedral above its body, a long narrow tail, and a bold clean WHITE patch on the rump at the base of the tail contrasting sharply against its brown back. Its face carries a distinct owl-like facial disc, a ruff of stiff feathers ringing the eyes giving it a round owlish expression rather than a plain flat hawk face. The white rump patch, the raised V wings and the owlish facial disc are essential: it must not be a broad-winged flat-gliding buzzard
snowyowl: A snowy owl, thick white plumage with sparse dark barring, bright yellow eyes, perched on snowy ground
barnowl: A barn owl, pale heart-shaped facial disc, golden-buff and white plumage, dark eyes, perched on a beam
greathornedowl: A great horned owl, mottled brown plumage, prominent feather tufts atop the head, large yellow eyes, perched on a branch
condor: An Andean condor, black plumage with a white neck ruff, bald pinkish-red head, perched on a rocky cliff
secretarybird: A secretary bird standing in profile, a tall ground-hunting bird of prey with EXTREMELY long slender bare crane-like legs making up most of its height, so it stands far taller than its body is deep, with pale grey plumage, black feathered thighs like shorts at the top of the legs, black flight feathers, two long central tail feathers trailing behind, a bare orange-red face, and a crest of long loose black quills sticking out behind its head like pens. Plain empty white background: no grey panel, no box, no oval, no shadow, no square backdrop, no border, no ground, no scenery of any kind behind the bird.
caracara: A crested caracara, black cap, pale neck, barred chest, bare orange facial skin, standing on the ground
goshawk: A northern goshawk, slate-grey back, finely barred pale chest, red eyes, perched on a branch
toucan: A toco toucan, glossy black body, white throat patch, enormous vivid orange curved beak, perched on a branch
kingfisher: A common kingfisher, vivid blue-green back, bright orange underside, long dagger-like beak, perched on a branch over water
peacock: An Indian peafowl, iridescent blue neck, elaborate green and gold train of eye-spotted tail feathers fanned out, standing on ground
quetzal: A resplendent quetzal, iridescent emerald-green plumage, crimson breast, extremely long trailing tail feathers, perched on a branch
lyrebird: A superb lyrebird, brown plumage, elaborate lyre-shaped tail feathers fanned out, standing on forest ground
hummingbird: A ruby-throated hummingbird, iridescent green back, males with a vivid red throat patch, needle-thin beak, hovering near a flower
crane: A red-crowned crane, white body plumage, black neck and secondary feathers, bare red crown patch, standing in a wetland
heron: A grey heron, slate-grey plumage, long white neck with a black stripe, long yellow dagger-like beak, standing in shallow water
stork: A white stork, white plumage with black wing feathers, long red legs and beak, standing in a marsh
shoebill: A shoebill, blue-grey plumage, enormous bulbous shoe-shaped beak, standing motionless in a swamp
pelican: A great white pelican standing in profile, a large white bird with a huge long orange bill carrying an enormous elastic throat pouch slung beneath it, a small head on a thick neck, black wingtips and short orange legs with webbed feet. Plain empty white background: no grey panel, no box, no square backdrop, no border, no ground, no scenery of any kind behind the bird.
spoonbill: A roseate spoonbill, vivid pink plumage, flat spoon-shaped grey beak, standing in shallow water
ibis: A scarlet ibis, vivid scarlet-red plumage, long curved thin beak, standing in a wetland
albatross: A wandering albatross, mostly white plumage with black wing edges, huge wingspan, pink hooked beak, standing on a windswept cliff
puffin: An Atlantic puffin, black and white plumage, large triangular orange-and-grey striped beak, standing on a rocky cliff
frigatebird: A magnificent frigatebird, glossy black plumage, long forked tail, males with a bright red inflatable throat pouch, perched on a branch
bluefootedbooby: A blue-footed booby, brown-and-white plumage, distinctive vivid blue webbed feet, standing on a rocky shore
ostrich: An ostrich, fluffy black-and-white plumage on males, long bare pink neck and legs, standing on savanna
emu: An emu, shaggy grey-brown plumage, long neck, standing tall on powerful legs
cassowary: A southern cassowary, glossy black plumage, tall bony helmet-like casque on the head, vivid blue and red neck skin, standing on forest floor
kiwi: A brown kiwi, round shaggy brown-streaked body, long thin downcurved beak, tiny vestigial wings, standing on forest floor
roadrunner: A greater roadrunner, streaked brown-and-white plumage, long tail, shaggy head crest, standing on desert ground
hoatzin: A hoatzin, spiky rust-colored crest, blue bare facial skin, brown-and-cream plumage, perched on a branch over water
kookaburra: A laughing kookaburra, brown-and-white plumage, large heavy beak, perched on a branch
potoo: A great potoo, mottled grey-brown bark-like plumage, huge yellow eyes, perched upright on a broken branch stump, camouflaged
mandarinduck: A mandarin duck, ornate orange sail-like feathers, purple breast, white eye stripe on a male, swimming on a pond
swan: A mute swan, pure white plumage, long curved neck, orange beak with a black knob, gliding on water
loon: A common loon, black-and-white checkered back, glossy black head with a striped neck band, swimming on a lake
emperorpenguin: An emperor penguin, black-and-white body with orange-yellow ear patches fading to pale yellow on the chest, standing upright on ice
woodpecker: A pileated woodpecker, mostly black plumage, bold white stripes on the face and neck, flaming red crest, clinging to a tree trunk
raven: A common raven, glossy all-black plumage, thick heavy beak, shaggy throat feathers, perched on a branch
honeybee: A honeybee, fuzzy amber-and-black striped body, translucent wings, perched on a flower
bumblebee: A bumblebee, round fuzzy black-and-yellow striped body, translucent wings, perched on a flower
orchidbee: An orchid bee, iridescent metallic green body, translucent wings, hovering near a flower
masonbee: A mason bee, metallic blue-black fuzzy body, translucent wings, perched on a flower
hoverfly: A hoverfly, slender body with bold yellow-and-black wasp-mimicking stripes, transparent wings, hovering near a flower
monarch: A monarch butterfly, vivid orange wings with bold black veins and white-spotted black borders, perched on a flower with wings open
sailfish: An Atlantic sailfish seen from the side, an elongated streamlined billfish with a long pointed spear-like bill, and an ENORMOUS sail-shaped dorsal fin running almost the entire length of its back and standing far taller than the body is deep, raised like a fan. Dark cobalt-blue above with a crisp silvery-white belly and rows of pale blue vertical bars along the flanks, with a stiff crescent tail
